title: Selecting elements
learningObjectives: Explain selecting elements and read or transform JavaScript data safely.

understand.concept: DOM selection methods include getElementById(), querySelector(), querySelectorAll(), and methods that return collections by tag or class. querySelector returns the first matching element or null; querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList of all matching elements.
understand.whyItMatters: Selecting the correct elements is the first step in safe DOM updates. Handle missing elements and understand whether a returned collection is live or static.
understand.analogy: A selector is a search pattern that identifies which nodes in the document tree should be retrieved.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript references, serialization, and DOM APIs have precise behaviour defined by the language and web platform.

explain.narrative: querySelector finds the first list item; querySelectorAll returns a NodeList containing all three list items.

examples.explanation: querySelector finds the first list item; querySelectorAll returns a NodeList containing all three list items.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the selected, transformed, or serialized data.

practise.guidedTask: Select a heading by ID, all cards by class, and one nested button. Handle a missing selector result safely.
practise.independentTask: Build a small data-processing or DOM-selection example. Include missing-data handling and explain any shallow-copy or serialization limits.
hints: Check optional properties before accessing them.
Remember shallow copies share nested references.
Handle JSON parsing errors and validate data shape.

questions.prompt: What does querySelector return when no element matches?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns null when there is no matching element.
